clue.text: Alpha females give public expression to romance

parts.note: alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, matching A
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural as in pp for pages
to air a view is to voice it in public

explanation.surface: Dominant women openly declaring their love for one another.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair is a romantic relationship, so a romance in that sense is an affair.

clue.text: Kingdom's motor-racing disrupted by gun going off

definitions.note: the 's is short for 'is', linking the definition; the kingdom is a biological division of living things

indicators.note: disrupted by says the first piece is broken open by the second

parts.note: F1, Formula One motor racing, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: going off says the letters of gun explode into a new order

explanation.surface: A country's Grand Prix interrupted by a gun firing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kingdom' suggests a country, but it is a biological kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologists class mushrooms, moulds and yeasts as a separate kingdom of living things.

clue.text: Union matching deal

definitions.meaning: a coming together in accord, harmony
correspondence between things, as between subject and verb in grammar
a pact or contract settled between parties

explanation.surface: A trade union striking a deal that matches the other side's offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Accord in opinion, grammatical concord and a settled contract are all called by this one word.

clue.text: Prompt Bolshevik saves time

indicators.note: saves says the first piece keeps the second inside it

parts.note: Bolsheviks were Communists, called Reds
MIN is the abbreviation for minute, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A quick-acting revolutionary buys a little time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like an adjective, quick, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt someone is to jog their memory, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Now one has majority support ——Hinge funny as Bracket

indicators.note: funny says the letters of hinge behave oddly and are rearranged

parts.note: a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A nod to Hinge and Bracket, a British drag comedy double act, with Hinge as funny as partner Bracket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' mixes TEE and HINGE together; 'as Bracket' only completes the double-act reference. UK law lowered the age of majority to this number in 1970.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the age of majority, when one legally becomes an adult, is this birthday.

clue.text: After a romantic meal prepared with unknown ingredient, kissing to start with this!

definitions.text: After a romantic meal prepared with unknown ingredient, kissing to start with this!

indicators.note: a meal prepared is cooked up, so its letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: X is the algebraic symbol for an unknown quantity

indicators.note: to start says only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: After a candlelit dinner with a mystery ingredient, starting to kiss would earn a punctuation mark of delight.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram covers A ROMANTIC MEAL plus X; the K of 'kissing' comes last. The whole clue is the scene that earns the mark it ends with.
explanation.definitionFit: The final symbol of the clue is the punctuation sign written for surprise or excitement.

clue.text: Most unsophisticated way to lend author support

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that lends support sits underneath the other

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: The simplest route by which a writer might be backed.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means naive or inexperienced, and this is its superlative.

clue.text: Beginner in truck on notice to put foot down

indicators.note: the beginner in a word is its first letter

parts.note: to read a notice is to take it in; here read stands for the act of noticing a written word

explanation.surface: A learner driver in a lorry is told to accelerate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put foot down' suggests speeding up or being firm, but means simply stepping.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is to step, setting one's foot on the ground.

clue.text: Sees new Latin translation as something necessary

indicators.note: new says the letters of sees are made over into a fresh order
a translation renders a word differently, so the letters of Latin are reworked

explanation.surface: A scholar considers a fresh rendering of a Latin text indispensable.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word has its own signal: 'new' makes ESSE from SEES and 'translation' makes NTIAL from LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An essential is a thing one cannot do without, a necessity.

clue.text: Hectored wife and mother pushed into rotten chore

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: pushed into says one piece is thrust inside the other
rotten says the letters of chore are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: MA is an everyday word for mother

explanation.surface: A bullied wife and mother is forced into some dreadful household task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hectored' is not bullied but belonging to Hector, the Trojan hero; 'rotten' rearranges CHORE to ROCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Andromache was married to Hector of Troy, so she is literally the wife Hector had.

clue.text: Worry about son's bearing

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to eat at someone is to worry or trouble them
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent fretting over how their boy carries himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like posture, but here it is a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass bearing is a direction, and one of the four cardinal points is that direction.

clue.text: Division in corporation to receive one billion for land once

indicators.note: to receive says the first piece takes the others into it

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a paunch; a rupture in the belly wall is a hernia
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A company splitting up so that a section can take on a billion in funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' suggests a company but is old slang for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernia is the Latin name the Romans used for Ireland, so it is a country's name from long ago.

clue.text: Cardinal making admission of a daughter —— her?

indicators.note: admitting something lets it inside, so the first piece holds the others

parts.note: a cardinal number such as nine

explanation.surface: A churchman confessing to having a daughter, and wondering who she might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a prince of the Church, but it is a cardinal number. The query in 'her?' flags that the girl's name is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadine is a girl's forename, so the pronoun for a woman is illustrated by one named example.

clue.text: Shock for commentators-runner coming into form

indicators.note: commentators speak to listeners, so the word is as heard on the radio

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair on the head

explanation.surface: A surprise for the broadcasters as an athlete suddenly finds peak fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' is not fitness but a hare's resting hollow in the grass, so the runner is the animal returning home.
explanation.definitionFit: The hare is a fast-running animal whose nest in long grass is called a form.

clue.text: Closely examine source of nuclear energy in plant

indicators.note: in says the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: anise is a plant grown for its aniseed
nuclear energy is released by splitting the atom

explanation.surface: Inspect the reactor at a power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a power station, but it is a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: To anatomise is to dissect or analyse something in minute detail.

clue.text: Mark my target when elite troops stray from path

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service
to sin is to stray from the path of righteousness

explanation.surface: A command to note a target when special forces go off course.
explanation.walkthrough: A mark is the victim chosen by a killer or con man, so 'Mark my target' is what a hired killer might say.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired killer has a victim, called a mark, so the phrase describes the speaker by what they hunt.

clue.text: Institution seen as above criticism, but lower in religion

definitions.meaning: an idea or body nobody is allowed to attack
a lower is something that moos, a cow, held holy in Hinduism

explanation.surface: A revered institution that nonetheless ranks lower in matters of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' reads as less high but is one who lows, or moos.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an untouchable institution comes from the cattle that Hindus revere and protect.

clue.text: Rested, holding artillery up: blunder in field leading to a British defeat

indicators.note: holding says the first piece keeps the second inside it

parts.note: sat means rested on a seat

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
OG is an own goal, a football blunder on the field
taken as written

explanation.surface: Troops resting with their guns raised, then a field mistake that leads to defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: OG means own goal, a football blunder; 'leading to' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: At Saratoga in 1777 a British army under Burgoyne surrendered to American forces.

clue.text: Players helping cricket side out — high scores for them?

parts.note: the players in a show are its cast

indicators.note: out says one piece is removed from another

parts.note: a helping or portion is a ration
the on side is one half of a cricket field (the other is the off side)

explanation.surface: Cricketers going out to help the team, with big totals in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes ON from RATION, leaving RATI. 'high scores' are musical parts written for very high voices, not runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrati were male singers who kept soprano or alto voices, so music pitched high was written for them.

clue.text: Everyone on about decision

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: C is the abbreviation of circa, Latin for about
everyone together is all

explanation.surface: Everybody weighing in on a ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee's call is a ruling or judgement made on the spot.

clue.text: You are texted by man politely pressing

parts.note: in text messages you are is shortened to UR
gent is short for gentleman, the polite word for a man

explanation.surface: A man courteously sending messages to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing matter is one that demands immediate attention.

clue.text: Old alumnus about to show concern for alcohol

indicators.note: about says the letters turn round and run backwards

parts.note: old means aged
OB is an old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former student about to reveal worry over someone's drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AGEDOB round. 'concern' is not worry but a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or bar, a business selling drink.

clue.text: Put out in Calais I put up with shocking treatment

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up says the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: Calais is in France, and the French for I is je
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, an electric shock treatment

explanation.surface: A traveller in Calais tolerating rough handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' looks like 'tolerated', but 'put up' reverses JE and 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject someone is to throw them out.

clue.text: Bottle good as weapon

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage, as in 'lost his bottle'

explanation.surface: A good bottle used as a weapon in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a glass object, but it is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve gas is a chemical weapon that attacks the nervous system.

clue.text: Biblical character among children badly raised

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
among says the name lies within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A figure from scripture who grew up among badly behaved children.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'among' in the definition, but it is the hidden-word signal. In a down clue 'raised' reads the letters from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: Abner was commander of Saul's army in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Military officer thought to have a first

indicators.note: the letter A is told to come first, moving from the end to the front

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: A soldier who believes he graduated with top honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a first' looks like a top degree; it tells the A at the end of IDEA to go to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is an officer who assists a senior commander, often shortened to aide.

clue.text: Shot of alcohol that is consumed in free time

indicators.note: consumed in says these pieces are swallowed inside another

parts.note: open can mean free, as in open access
ale is an alcoholic drink
SC (scilicet) is Latin shorthand for namely, that is

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a measure of spirits but means shot through with changing colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot silk shimmers with shifting colours, and opalescent means showing that milky play of colour like an opal.

clue.text: Gave up financial job in artists' quarter

parts.note: to leave a job is to give it up, so left means gave up
to bank money is a task in managing one's finances

explanation.surface: Someone who quit work in finance to live among painters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Left Bank of the Seine in Paris is famed as the district of artists and writers.

clue.text: Fox provides coverage for conflict once in progress

indicators.note: covering something wraps around it, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: tod is an old and dialect word for a fox
a war is a conflict
